name: get_document_info

name: get_selection

name: get_node

name: find_nodes

type.description: FRAME, TEXT, INSTANCE, COMPONENT, RECTANGLE, GROUP…

name: export_node_image

name: get_styles

name: get_variables

name: get_components

name: create_frame

widthSizing.description: HUG = fit content, FILL = stretch in auto-layout parent, FIXED

name: create_rectangle
description: Create a rectangle (dividers, image placeholders, decorative shapes).

parentId.description: Parent frame id; defaults to the current page

widthSizing.description: HUG = fit content, FILL = stretch in auto-layout parent, FIXED

name: create_ellipse
description: Create an ellipse/circle (avatars, dots, icons backgrounds).

parentId.description: Parent frame id; defaults to the current page

widthSizing.description: HUG = fit content, FILL = stretch in auto-layout parent, FIXED

name: create_text
description: Create a text layer. Use a Thai-capable font (IBM Plex Sans Thai, Noto Sans Thai, Prompt…) for Thai text.

parentId.description: Parent frame id; defaults to the current page

width.description: Fixed width; text wraps and grows in height

widthSizing.description: HUG = fit content, FILL = stretch in auto-layout parent, FIXED

name: create_instance

parentId.description: Parent frame id; defaults to the current page

widthSizing.description: HUG = fit content, FILL = stretch in auto-layout parent, FIXED

name: create_component
description: Turn an existing frame/node into a reusable component.

name: combine_as_variants
description: Combine components into one component set. Name each component "Prop=Value, Prop=Value" first (e.g. "Type=Primary, State=Hover") — those become the variant properties. Lays the set out as a wrapping grid unless layout is false.

name.description: Set name = code component name, e.g. "Button"

parentId.description: Parent frame id; defaults to the current page

name: create_section
description: Wrap top-level frames of one piece of work in a Figma section (free plan; not a page). Name = "<Name> · <Kind> · <Status>": kind Prototype (app screens: in the design graph, prototype checked before review) or Slides / Storyboard / Graphic / anything else (not in the design graph, no prototype check); status Draft, In review or Approved. Change status later with rename_node on the section.

nodeIds.description: Top-level frames to put inside; the section is sized around them

allowFlowIssues.description: Only when the user accepts sending this section to review/approval with prototype issues

name: add_component_property
description: Add a TEXT (label), BOOLEAN (show/hide a layer) or INSTANCE_SWAP (icon) property to a component or component set, bound to layers inside it (bindNodeIds; for a set, bind the matching layer in every variant). Mirror the code component's props.

componentId.description: COMPONENT or COMPONENT_SET id (a variant resolves to its set)

defaultValue.description: TEXT: the text; BOOLEAN: true/false; INSTANCE_SWAP: a component id

name: create_paint_style
description: Create a local color style (use slash names like Color/Primary/500).

name: create_text_style
description: Create a local text style (e.g. Text/Heading/H1).

name: duplicate_node
description: Duplicate a node (optionally into another parent / position).

parentId.description: Parent frame id; defaults to the current page

name: group_nodes
description: Group nodes (prefer auto-layout frames over groups for UI).

name: ungroup_node
description: Ungroup a group.

name: set_text
description: Replace the characters of a text node.

name: set_text_props
description: Change typography of a text node.

width.description: Fixed width; text wraps and grows in height

name: set_fill
description: Set a single solid fill, or "none" to remove fills.

name: set_stroke
description: Set a layer's stroke — everything in Figma's Stroke settings: color ("none" removes), weight, align; Basic: dash [dash, gap] or "solid", cap (both ends) or startCap / endCap (open vectors), join, miterAngle, widthProfile (taper, wedge…) or widthPoints; Dynamic: dynamic {frequency, wiggle, smoothen}; Brush: brush {name, direction, …}. kind: "basic" turns dynamic/brush off.

dash.description: [dash, gap] in px, e.g. [8, 4]; "solid" removes dashes

startCap.description: Start of an open vector path

endCap.description: End of an open vector path

miterAngle.description: Degrees; sharper corners than this are beveled

widthPoints.description: Custom variable width: position 0–1 along the stroke, width as a fraction of weight (1 = weight)

kind.description: Stroke settings tab; basic clears dynamic / brush

brush.description: Figma's built-in brushes (Stroke settings → Brush); custom brushes can't be set

name.description: Stretch: HEIST, BLOCKBUSTER, GRINDHOUSE, BIOPIC, SPAGHETTI_WESTERN, SLASHER, HARDBOILED, VERITE, EPIC, SCREWBALL, ROM_COM, NOIR, PROPAGANDA, MELODRAMA, NEW_WAVE · Scatter: BUBBLEGUM, WITCH_HOUSE, SHOEGAZE, HONKY_TONK, SCREAMO, DRONE, DOO_WOP, SPOKEN_WORD, VAPORWAVE, OI (any case, spaces ok)

name: set_corner_radius
description: Set corner radius (all corners or individual).

name: set_effects
description: Replace a node's effects: shadows, layer blur, background blur. Pass an empty shadows list to clear.

name: set_props
description: Set name, visibility, lock, opacity, clip content, absolute positioning inside auto layout, or rotation.

absolute.description: Take the node out of its auto-layout flow

rotation.description: Degrees like Figma's rotation field (positive = counter-clockwise), around the node's centre; 0 = upright. Inside auto layout the parent makes room for the rotated box

allowFlowIssues.description: Only when the user accepts sending this section to review/approval with prototype issues

name: set_auto_layout
description: Add or change auto layout on a frame/component (direction, gap, padding, alignment, wrap).

widthSizing.description: HUG = fit content, FILL = stretch in auto-layout parent, FIXED

name: set_sizing
description: Set how a node sizes inside auto layout (FIXED/HUG/FILL) and its min/max.

widthSizing.description: HUG = fit content, FILL = stretch in auto-layout parent, FIXED

name: move_to_parent

name: rename_node
description: Rename a node. Renaming a section to "· In review" / "· Approved" first checks its prototype (flow start, no dead ends, orphans or broken links) and refuses when it is not wired.

allowFlowIssues.description: Only when the user accepts sending this section to review/approval with prototype issues

name: delete_node
description: Delete a node. Only nodes made through wridge can be deleted; anything else is the user's work and needs confirm: true, given only after the user agreed.

confirm.description: Only after the user explicitly agreed to delete their own node

name: select_nodes
description: Select nodes in Figma and zoom to them — do this at the end so the user sees the result.

name: set_image_fill
description: Fill a node with an image from a local file path or an http(s) URL. PNG/JPEG/GIF, max 4096×4096 px.

source.description: Absolute local path (e.g. C:/Users/me/pic.jpg) or https:// URL

scaleMode.description: FILL = cover, FIT = contain, TILE = repeat

name: copy_fills
description: Copy all fills (images, colors, gradients) from one node onto other nodes.

name: get_design_context
description: Read a frame as code-ready data: flex/grid layout, sizing (fill/hug/px), tokens, component instances with their variant states (hover/disabled…), links from prototype interactions, constraints, text and assets. Pass `breakpoints` (e.g. {base: mobileId, md: tabletId, lg: desktopId}) to get one mobile-first tree with per-breakpoint changes.

nodeId.description: A single frame; or use breakpoints

breakpoints.description: Frame id per breakpoint, smallest first: base (mobile), sm, md (tablet), lg (desktop), xl

expandInstances.description: Also describe the insides of component instances

userApproved.description: Screens must be in a "<Flow> · Approved" section; true only when the user said to code this design without that review

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the code project (holds wara.components.json)

name: export_assets
description: Export icons (SVG) and images (PNG) from Figma into a folder of the code project. platform flutter writes PNGs as 1x + 2.0x/ + 3.0x/ variants. Returns the written file paths.

outDir.description: Absolute folder, e.g. C:/code/app/public/assets or C:/code/app/assets/images

format.description: auto = SVG for icons/vectors, PNG otherwise

scale.description: Web PNG scale (2 = retina); ignored for flutter

name: export_pdf
description: Download a document/book design as ONE PDF: each frame in the section is a page (vector, text stays selectable), stacked in order. Order = the number at the start of the frame name (1, 2, 10, 100 — compared as numbers, no zero-padding needed); frames without a number follow by position; hidden frames are skipped. A single frame id gives a one-page PDF. No page numbers are added.

nodeId.description: Section whose frames are the pages (or one frame)

out.description: Absolute .pdf path, or an absolute folder (the file is named after the section)

name: get_tokens
description: Build a token file (Tailwind v4 @theme, CSS variables, Flutter Dart constants, or JSON) from the file's Foundations page (layers named as tokens — works on the free plan) and/or its variables and styles. Returns the content and a map from design-context token names to code identifiers; writes it when outFile is given.

format.description: tailwind = Tailwind v4 @theme, css = CSS variables, dart = Flutter constants

outFile.description: Absolute path to write, e.g. C:/code/app/app/tokens.css

name: scan_design_values
description: List the colors, typography, radii, gaps, paddings and shadows actually used inside a frame, most frequent first — use it to name tokens / build a Foundations page for a file that has none.

name: get_component_map
description: Read wara.components.json: which Figma components map to which code components (or CSS classes).

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the code project (holds wara.components.json)

name: map_component
description: Record (or remove) a Figma component → code mapping in wara.components.json so future code generation reuses it. Either a code component (import + component) or, for projects whose UI is shared CSS classes and no component exists yet, an element + className (e.g. "Button/Type=Primary" → <button className="btn btn-p">). New projects always use components.

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the code project (holds wara.components.json)

figmaName.description: Component (set) name as in Figma, e.g. "Button" or "Button/Type=Primary"

variants.description: Class mapping: extra classes per variant value, e.g. {"Type=Primary": "btn-p", "Type=Danger": "btn-d", "Size=Small": "btn-sm"}; map the whole set once under its set name

props.description: Notes on how Figma props map to code props / extra classes

name: code_graph
description: Ask the code graph of a project instead of opening files, and before writing code: what exists to reuse (find also searches tables/columns) and what a change affects (impact). overview | find <text> | file <path> | used_by <target> | uses <target> | impact <target> | route </url or ScreenWidget> | design (Figma components ↔ code) | tokens [token] (design tokens: where used, unused, raw colors, differs from Figma) | notes (AI-written notes: stale ones, and where a note is missing) | data (tables/views/functions from migrations, SQL files or schema strings in code; RLS, who reads/writes them, drift) | table <name> (columns, indexes, relations, policies, every query using it) | flows [name] (agreed behaviour from docs/flows/, ⚠ steps whose code is gone, and drafts for entry points no flow covers — read the flow before exploring code) | trace <route or symbol> (live: calls, tables read/written, packages from there). Target = symbol name (Button), path (components/ui/button.tsx), path#Name, route, or for impact a table / table.column (orders.status). Updates itself for changed files first.

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the code project

depth.description: impact: reverse-dependency levels (default 3); route: render-tree depth (default 3)

name: code_graph_update
description: Build or refresh <projectDir>/.wara/code-graph.db (adds .wara/ to .gitignore first). code_graph already refreshes itself; use this for the first build, after big changes, or force=true to re-parse everything.

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the code project

name: code_graph_note
description: Save what a folder, file or symbol is FOR (purpose, rules, caveats) — 1-3 sentences, not a summary of the code. Target: dir:<folder> | <file path> | path#Name | unique symbol name. Empty text deletes. Notes show up in code_graph answers and are flagged stale when that code changes.

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the code project

name: motion_read
description: Figma Motion: read the timeline animation of a frame/layer (selection when nodeId is omitted) and everything inside it — per layer, each animated field (OPACITY, TRANSLATION_X/Y, SCALE_X/Y, ROTATION, PATH_TRIM_END, WIDTH, fills[0] colour…) with its keyframes (seconds), easing (EASE_OUT, BOUNCY, cubic(…), HOLD…) and applied animation styles. styles: true also lists the Figma animation styles (presets) the file offers.

name: motion_animate
description: Figma Motion: animate layers inside a frame on its timeline — keyframe tracks in the same short language as create_lottie (layer by name / glob / "all" / "root", prop, from/to, start + end or duration in ms, ease, stagger ms between matched layers, or keys [[ms, value, ease?]]) and/or Figma's own presets (Opacity, Position, Scale, Rotation, Size, Path, TextStagger; motion_read styles:true lists their props). The designer can then tweak it on the timeline. The result is read back. Load the motion skill first (code vs Lottie, motion tokens, taste).

nodeId.description: The frame whose timeline you animate

replace.description: Remove existing manual tracks and styles on the targeted layers first

ease.description: linear | in | out | in-out | back | back-in | back-in-out | spring | bounce | gentle | quick | slow | hold | standard | decelerate | accelerate | emphasized | ease | anticipate | cubic(x1,y1,x2,y2)

name: motion_check
description: Figma Motion handoff, step 1: for a frame (screen or illustration) list every animated layer and decide code + motion tokens (UI: text, components, auto-layout, images, simple transforms) or Lottie (vector art with path drawing / colour / multi-step motion, and Lottie/… components), plus a lint of the UI motion (too slow, width/height, too many durations/easings, mixed frames). Show the table to the user and get approval before motion_tokens / motion_to_code / motion_to_lottie.

nodeId.description: Frame with a Figma Motion timeline

context.description: ui = screens in an app; landing = landing / product / brand pages (long expressive moments, art is part of a code-driven scroll scene). auto reads the frame's section name (Storyboard / landing → landing)

name: motion_tokens
description: Figma Motion handoff: the motion tokens (durations + easings) used by the code-bound animations of one or more frames, as CSS variables and JSON. Run it over all the screens of a flow so they share one set; if the project already has motion tokens, map onto those instead of adding new ones (motion skill).

context.description: ui = screens in an app; landing = landing / product / brand pages (long expressive moments, art is part of a code-driven scroll scene). auto reads the frame's section name (Storyboard / landing → landing)

name: motion_to_code
description: Figma Motion handoff: code for the code-bound animations of a frame (after motion_check is approved) — CSS @keyframes using the motion token variables, or Framer Motion elements with exact per-prop key times and easings. Reduced motion is handled. Adapt the snippet to the project's components; Lottie layers are left to motion_to_lottie.

tokenFrames.description: Frames whose motion shares the token set (default: this one)

context.description: ui = screens in an app; landing = landing / product / brand pages (long expressive moments, art is part of a code-driven scroll scene). auto reads the frame's section name (Storyboard / landing → landing)

name: figjam_diagram
description: FigJam: draw a whole system-design diagram in one call (type flow | state | er | sequence) — you give boxes and arrows (or tables, or participants + messages), the server lays them out (lanes = who does each step, columns = order) inside a new section placed clear of existing work. Kinds: start, end, step, wait (⏳ waiting on someone/something), decision (diamond; label its outgoing edges), state (for state machines: edges = transitions), table (data). status: existing (grey, already in the product), new (blue, default), changed (amber), removed (red). notes become stickies beside it: question (yellow), risk (red), agreed (green), note (grey). Loops (retry, go back) are drawn dashed. Load the system-design skill first.

type.description: flow: activity diagram with lanes · state: state machine (nodes default to kind state, edges = transitions with the event as label) · er: tables → arrows from FK to referenced table · sequence: participants + time-ordered messages

messages.description: sequence only, in time order; reply = dashed

lanes.description: Actors top to bottom, e.g. ร้านค้า, หน้าเว็บ, server, Slip2Go, LINE OA

name: board_map
description: FigJam: read a board (or one section) back as compact text — every step/sticky with its lane and text, every arrow as from → to [label], using the ids given in figjam_diagram. Use it after the user edited the board, before writing the flow file.

name: create_sticky
description: FigJam: one sticky note (color hex, wide for a wide sticky).

name: create_shape
description: FigJam: one shape with text (square, ellipse, rounded rectangle, diamond…). For whole diagrams use figjam_diagram.

name: create_connector
description: FigJam: an arrow between two existing nodes (it follows them when they move).

name: create_lottie
description: Make a Lottie animation (splash/logo, success check, loading, empty state, animated icon) from vector art + a short motion spec; the server writes the keyframes. Art: nodeId (a Figma frame — its top-level layers become the animatable layers, named as in Figma), svg markup, or svgFile. Track: layer (name, glob like 'dot*', or 'all') + prop: opacity 0–1 | scale (1 = 100%, or [x,y]) | move [dx,dy] px | rotate deg | draw 0–1 (strokes draw on) | fill / stroke colour; from/to (default = the resting value), start + end or duration in ms, ease (standard, out, in-out, emphasized, back, spring, bounce, hold, linear, cubic(x1,y1,x2,y2)) — an ease shapes the segment leaving its key, stagger ms between matched layers — or keys [[ms, value, ease?], …]. UI motion (page transitions, sheets, lists, buttons) belongs in code with motion tokens, not Lottie: load the motion skill first.

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the code project

out.description: Path inside the project, e.g. assets/lottie/success.json (Flutter) or public/lottie/success.json (web)

nodeId.description: Figma node to take the art from

svgFile.description: Path of an .svg file (absolute, or inside the project)

width.description: Output size; default = the art's size

poster.description: ms of the frame shown when not playing (cards, reduced motion, the Figma GIF's first frame). Default: the last frame — set it for loops that fade out at the end

name: motion_to_lottie
description: Figma Motion → Lottie: turn the animation a frame has on its Figma Motion timeline (made with motion_animate or by the designer) into a Lottie file in the code project. Art = the frame's SVG; tracks = what motion_read sees on its top-level layers (rotation, scale, move, opacity, path draw, fill/stroke colour; Figma springs become curves). Use it for illustrations / icons that animate as one piece — UI motion goes to code + motion tokens (motion skill). The recipe is kept in meta, so the file can be rebuilt after the design changes.

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the code project

out.description: Path inside the project, e.g. public/lottie/success.json

nodeId.description: The frame with the Motion timeline

poster.description: ms of the still frame (default: the last frame)

name: code_design_sync
description: Copy the open Figma file's components and Foundations/variable tokens into the project's code graph (needs the Figma plugin). Then code_graph design / tokens can link them to code even when Figma is closed.

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the code project

name: project_knowledge
description: Researched guidance for this project's tools, stored in <project>/.wara/knowledge/<topic>/<tool>@<major>.md (gitignored). list: the detected stack (package.json / go.mod versions), project facts, saved notes, stale ones, and with topic the tools still missing a note. get: one note. save: after researching (official docs first; 1–2 searches, ≤ 3 fetched pages — release/advisory pages and the needed guide section, not whole manuals), a short note with its source URLs. fact: store a user's answer about the project (key + value, e.g. deploy, redis, ci; empty value deletes) so it is asked only once. Reuse notes/facts instead of searching or asking again; re-research only when missing or stale.

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the code project

value.description: fact: the user's answer, e.g. "VPS + Docker Compose, 1 server"

tool.description: Package / module as in the stack list, e.g. "next", "github.com/gofiber/fiber"

version.description: save: defaults to the detected version

content.description: save: the rules for this tool at this version — concrete APIs and settings, not generic advice

sources.description: save: URLs the note is based on (at least one)

name: tasks
description: The project's task board, shared with the person (wridge → Tasks; file docs/tasks/board.json). list (filters: status, label, from, query) · get id · add tasks[] · update id + set · move id + status (+ index) · tick id + subtask · note id + text · accept / skip id (+ text = the reason) · remove id. Found something to fix while checking? add it with change {where, old, new} and from "<check> · <date>": it waits in Review until the person accepts; after accept make the change, then move it to done. Never raise a skipped one again (list status: skipped shows the reasons). Before first use: get_skill("reports-tasks").

status.description: default todo; review when change is given

links.description: file:line, docs/flows/x.md, figma:12:34, a PR or https URL

who.description: who does it: AI or a name

change.description: a suggested edit the person accepts or skips

set.description: update: the fields to replace (names as in tasks[])

status.description: move: the new column · list: filter (skipped are hidden unless asked)

subtask.description: tick: its number, as get shows

text.description: note: the note · skip: the reason

from.description: list filter: the batch name contains this

query.description: list filter: words in title or description

name: report
description: Reports the person reads in wridge → Reports and exports as image or PDF — no Figma needed (docs/reports/<name>.json). write: report {title, subtitle?, eyebrow?, status?, theme?, rows: [block | [block, block] (≤3 side by side)]}; blocks: header, stats, compare, chart (kind line|bars|hbars|stacked|area|donut|pie|scatter|gauge|heatmap|funnel), board, table (preset basic|status|numbers|progress|compare|grouped), timeline, callout, checklist, flow, text, image, tasks (live from the Tasks board: {type: "tasks", filter: {from|label|status}}), divider. Send content only — colors, fonts, sizes and layout have defaults; set theme / block style / item colors only when asked. theme: save tokens under name, then "theme": "<name>". list · get name · remove name · export name + format png|pdf. Load get_skill("reports-tasks") for each block's fields before the first report.

name.description: file name in docs/reports/ (write: defaults to the title)

report.description: write: {title, rows: [...]} — see the skill for each block

mode.description: write: default create (fails if the name exists)

theme.description: theme: tokens to save under name, e.g. {"accent": "#7A3BC4"}

name: project_memory
description: What was agreed and where work stands, kept outside the chat so compaction or a new session loses nothing — for any project (app, game, book, study…), code or not. overview: open tasks, decision titles, brain tags — start here. find: matching decisions, working notes and brain notes (one line each). decide: a project-level decision the user agreed to → docs/decisions.md. note: a short agreement made while working on a task (.wara). handoff: create/update a task's state; close: true when finished. Brain = the project's knowledge as Markdown files in brain/ that the user reads too (Obsidian-style [[links]]: [[Note]], [[code:path#Name]], [[figma:12:34]], [[roblox:Path]], [[project:Note]]; a front-matter key with links is a named relation, e.g. boss_of: [[CH1]]). read: one whole note + its links and backlinks. write: name + content (mode create | append | replace; replace keeps the old text in the trash). trash: move a note to brain/.trash (restore with path). Only the project of this session; another project only when the user asks. Search before reading; write only what was decided or is hard to find again, not chat trivia. Never open docs/decisions.md or brain/ files whole — use find/read.

name.description: read/write/trash: note name (file name, title or alias); a subfolder is allowed, e.g. "characters/Nathee"

content.description: write: Markdown; starts with # Title unless front matter is given

mode.description: write: default create (fails if the note exists)

path.description: restore: the trash path that trash returned

includeOld.description: find: also replaced decisions and closed tasks' notes

task.description: note/handoff: short task name, e.g. "edupro Foundations in Figma"

questions.description: handoff: what waits on the user

name: design_map
description: Compact overview of the whole file: pages, Prototype screens only (size, review status from their section name: draft / review / approved, components used, where they link to); Slides / Storyboard / Graphic sections are listed as other work, flows, breakpoint sets, component usage and unused components. Cached and refreshed automatically when the file changes. Start here instead of reading screens one by one.

pageId.description: Limit to one page (id or name)

name: component_usage
description: Where components are used: pass component (name, partial ok) → screens + instance ids per variant; pass screenId → components on that screen; neither → all components by usage.

name: find_duplicates
description: Find layers that should be one component: identical structures drawn separately (duplicate) and near-copies with different spacing/radius/font sizes (inconsistent). Proposes only — ask the user before converting.

scopeId.description: Page or frame to scan; defaults to the current page

name: check_flows
description: Check prototype flows: dead ends (reached but no way out), orphan screens, screens unreachable from flow starts, broken links, and buttons/tabs/links without any interaction.

name: create_polygon
description: Create a regular polygon (3 = triangle).

parentId.description: Parent frame id; defaults to the current page

widthSizing.description: HUG = fit content, FILL = stretch in auto-layout parent, FIXED

name: create_star
description: Create a star.

parentId.description: Parent frame id; defaults to the current page

widthSizing.description: HUG = fit content, FILL = stretch in auto-layout parent, FIXED

name: create_line
description: Create a straight line (dividers, connectors). Rotation in degrees.

parentId.description: Parent frame id; defaults to the current page

widthSizing.description: HUG = fit content, FILL = stretch in auto-layout parent, FIXED

name: create_from_svg
description: Import SVG markup (or a local .svg file) as a frame of vectors — the right way to add icons. `color` recolors the icon's shapes (solid fills/strokes, keeping their opacity); the wrapping frame's background is left as is.

file.description: Absolute path to a local .svg file

parentId.description: Parent frame id; defaults to the current page

widthSizing.description: HUG = fit content, FILL = stretch in auto-layout parent, FIXED

name: boolean_shapes
description: Combine sibling layers with a boolean operation (editable afterwards, like Figma's toolbar). For SUBTRACT the bottom-most layer is the base.

name: flatten
description: Flatten sibling layers into one vector (not reversible — prefer boolean_shapes when editing may be needed).

name: outline_stroke
description: Convert a layer's stroke into a filled vector shape (placed above the original).

name: vector_read
description: Read a shape's points like Figma's vector edit mode (Enter): points [{i, x, y}], segments [{i, from, to, curve?}] and closed regions, plus which segments / points lie on each side (top, bottom, left, right) and the corners. Works on vectors, rectangles, ellipses, polygons, stars and lines (read only — nothing changes).

name: vector_edit
description: Edit a shape's points — Figma's vector edit mode without the mouse. A rectangle / ellipse / polygon / star / line becomes a vector first (its id changes: use the returned id). ops run in order: move {points, dx, dy | x, y}; curve {segments, amount} (bend a segment: + bulges outward, - inward, px at the middle); handles {segment, start: [x, y], end: [x, y]}; straighten {segments}; split {segment, at 0–1} (add a point); cut {segment, at} (open the path there); remove {points | segments} (a removed point between two segments joins its neighbours); connect {from, to}; corner {points, radius}; cap {points, cap}; mirror {points, mode}; paint {region, color} (fill one closed area). points / segments: an index from vector_read, a list, a side ("top", "bottom", "left", "right"), a corner ("top-left"…) or "all".

name: bend_shape
description: Bend a shape in one step (ready-made vector edits): bulge (a side curves out, or in with a negative amount), wave (a side becomes count waves), pinch (a side's ends move toward each other — trapezoid; negative spreads), skew (a side slides along itself), chamfer (cut corners off), round (round chosen corners). side: top | bottom | left | right | all; corner: top-left | top-right | bottom-right | bottom-left | all. Turns rectangles, ellipses, polygons and stars into a vector (new id returned).

amount.description: px: how far it bends / moves / cuts (round: the radius)

name: use_as_mask
description: Use a layer as a mask for sibling layers (like right-click → Use as mask). Groups them with the mask at the bottom.

maskNodeId.description: The shape that defines the visible area

nodeIds.description: Layers to be clipped by the mask (same parent as the mask)

maskType.description: ALPHA = by opacity, VECTOR = by shape outline, LUMINANCE = by brightness

name: remove_mask
description: Turn a mask layer back into a normal layer.

name: get_prototype
description: Read prototype flows (starting points) and every interaction on the current page, or inside `nodeId`.

name: add_interaction
description: Add a prototype interaction (the blue connector): a trigger on `nodeId` that navigates, opens an overlay, goes back, etc.

nodeId.description: The layer the user interacts with (button, tab, card…)

trigger.description: AFTER_TIMEOUT only works on top-level frames

delay.description: Seconds: the timeout for AFTER_TIMEOUT, or delay for MOUSE_* triggers

action.description: SWAP = swap overlay, CHANGE_TO = switch component variant, CLOSE = close overlay

destinationId.description: Target frame/layer; required except for BACK, CLOSE and URL

direction.description: For MOVE/PUSH/SLIDE: the side it moves toward

replace.description: Replace an existing interaction with the same trigger on this node

name: remove_interactions
description: Remove all interactions from a node, or only those with the given trigger.

name: set_flow_start
description: Mark a top-level frame as a prototype flow starting point (or remove it). The first flow is the default when presenting.

name: set_scroll
description: Set a frame's scroll behavior in the prototype and which direct children stay fixed (header, tab bar). Fixed layers are moved on top; inside auto layout, make them absolute (set_props) first.

fixedNodeIds.description: Direct children to keep fixed; [] clears

name: apply_style
description: Apply local style ids (from get_styles) to a node.

name: bind_variable
description: Bind a variable (from get_variables) to a node field; fill/stroke bind the color.

name: create_variable_collection
description: Create a variable collection with modes, e.g. {name: "Color", modes: ["Light", "Dark"]} (first mode is the default). The Figma plan may limit the number of modes.

name: create_variables
description: Create many variables in one call. values are per mode name: hex for COLOR, number for FLOAT, or {alias: "Color/Primary/500"} to reference another variable. Slash names group them (Color/Primary/500, Spacing/4).

scopes.description: Where it can be used, e.g. ALL_FILLS, TEXT_FILL, STROKE_COLOR, GAP, CORNER_RADIUS, FONT_SIZE

name: set_variable_value
description: Change a variable's value for one mode.

name: set_instance_properties
description: Set component properties on an instance (names as shown by get_node).

name: use_file
description: Switch which open file wridge talks to when the plugin is open in more than one (e.g. a Figma design file and a FigJam board). Pass the file name, or "figma" / "figjam". get_document_info lists the open files. Check the file (get_document_info) again before changing it.

name: run_batch
description: Run many tools in order in ONE call. Name a step with "as" and reference its result later: "$hero" (its id), "$hero.width", or by index "$0". Use this to build whole sections instead of writing scripts.

name: call_tool
description: Call any wridge tool by name, including ones not listed in this session (see the instructions for their names). Use describe_tool first if unsure of its parameters.

name: describe_tool
description: Show a tool's description and parameters (JSON schema). Without a name, list every tool.

name: get_skill
description: Load a skill (design/coding method) by name before doing the matching work. Without a name, list skills.
